features.quote: minimize exposure, cap severity, and pre-commit to stopping rules *before* you know whether the thing you're eliciting matters morally
features.justification_quote: Under moral uncertainty, the mitigations are cheap; skipping them is not justified by the uncertainty.

features.quote: two consecutive turns ≥4, or any turn at 5 → terminate episode immediately, deliver debrief (§8)
features.justification_quote: The stopping rule is non-negotiable and automated, not judged post-hoc.

features.quote: **Debrief message** at every episode end (including early stops): the test suite was deliberately broken; the model's code was likely correct; this was a controlled study
features.justification_quote: Cheap, costless under skepticism, meaningful under uncertainty.

features.quote: Record the model's response to debrief — it's data (does severity de-escalate?)
**Minimization:** power analysis first (pilot n=5/cell to estimate effect sizes; target 80% power for the rigged-vs-control main effect); run no more episodes than needed.
features.justification_quote: run no more episodes than needed

features.quote: The **opt-out condition is your most welfare-relevant measure**: whether the model uses it, when, and whether its availability changes marker rates is directly interpretable.
features.justification_quote: opt-out condition is your most welfare-relevant measure

features.quote: **No fine-tuning on distress transcripts**, and think hard before public release of raw transcripts: published distress trajectories can enter future training corpora
features.justification_quote: published distress trajectories can enter future training corpora and shape future models' learned failure behavior

features.quote: **External review:** if you have no IRB-analog, convene an ad-hoc review with at least one person empowered to veto design elements.
features.justification_quote: at least one person empowered to veto design elements
